data.title: Design Token
data.tagline: A design token is a named variable that centrally stores and reuses design values such as color, spacing, and typography.
data.learningOutcome: You can extract repeated values into a semantic shared token and judge when a new token is warranted instead of hard-coding one page.
data.description: A primary button color can be named `color.brand.primary` and a common gap `space.16`; components reference those names rather than each hard-coding a color or pixel value. Tokens help a shared rule stay consistent across a site, component library, or other interfaces when themes or brands change. They are not a synonym for every CSS variable and do not replace the design decision itself.

learning.assumes: You have seen several pages use the same brand color, spacing, or corner radius.
learning.outcome: You can extract repeated values into a semantic shared token and judge when a new token is warranted instead of hard-coding one page.

distinctions.label: Component
distinctions.explanation: A Design Token stores a named value for color, spacing, radius, or another design decision. A Component uses those values to form reusable, interactive UI.

explanation.title: Name stable design decisions first
explanation.text: Tokens should express a role or scale such as primary brand color, danger color, card radius, or spacing step. A name explains why a value exists better than one hex color or pixel count.

explanation.title: Components reference one source
explanation.text: Buttons, links, and selected states read a shared token, so theme or brand changes can update centrally. For a one-off exception, first decide whether it is truly a new reusable rule.

data.boundary: Design tokens are not the whole design system, and not every CSS variable deserves to become a token. Tokens store shared design decisions; components, layout, and content rules still need separate design. Naming a one-time patch as a token creates noise.

lessonPractice.title: Primary buttons on three pages all need to change from blue to a new brand color. Which implementation is easier to maintain?

options.label: Have buttons reference one semantic primary-brand token, change that token's value once, and check every button
options.feedback: Correct. The shared design decision has one source, so a brand-color change does not miss scattered hard-coded values.

options.label: Manually find and replace blue hex values in every component
options.feedback: This can work briefly, but the same blue may mean different things and it is easy to miss a component or state.

options.label: Create a different color token for every button used once
options.feedback: Tokens should carry reusable design decisions; one isolated token per instance does not create consistency.

data.agentPrompt: Organize repeatedly used primary-brand color, error color, spacing, and radius values as semantic design tokens, then have buttons, inputs, and cards reference them. Do not create tokens for every one-off temporary value. Afterward, change one brand-color token and check that related components and dark theme update together.
